decision: Present unaccepted legacy IBus completion hints as standard auxiliary text; reserve legacy document preedit for the typed owned composition.
reason: The pinned Firefox 157 TextComposition commit request saves mLastData before notifying the native IME and may restore/synthesize it after an empty reset response. Therefore a display-only suffix in document preedit can be committed on blur. A Reset-only adapter repair is rejected before implementation.
supersedes: The legacy presentation compatibility clause of 2026-10-04-preedit-suggestion-visual-boundary; preserve typed neutral styling and the atomic protocol.
verification: Planned: legacy candidate publication RED; owned/committed text conservation, separate display lifecycle and stale/failure controls, exact current Tab and unchanged atomic proposal proof; remote affected closure and independent review; native Firefox/Chrome ten-field plans, visible panel and latency, followed by separate Plasma acceptance.
not_tested: Changed code, changed-byte native behavior, panel visibility/position, latency and Plasma acceptance remain NOT_TESTED at decision time.

consequences.scope: Same LayIbusEngine/EngineOutput owner, same IBus connection and standard UpdateAuxiliaryText signal. No new document-edit delivery, executor, reducer, authority, cache or client-specific bypass. See TD-156 preflight for full consequence analysis.
consequences.authority: Keep actual preedit visibility distinct from auxiliary visibility. Existing candidates, current frame/owner, verified Tab, model generations and feedback remain authoritative. Display failure retires selectable candidates.
consequences.compatibility: Legacy committed-tail and owned-word candidates use auxiliary presentation. Manual owned-word layout edits keep existing preedit. Atomic output has no auxiliary capability and retains its original proposal protocol and behavior; no out-of-transaction display or universal atomic repair claim.
consequences.cost: No waits or deadlines grow. At most one bounded auxiliary update per candidate publication; suffix-only publication no longer starts a document composition. No workers, timers, queues or model/data changes. Native speed and panel support remain gates. Two existing async output boundaries are heap-pinned to bound nested key/lifecycle future sizes. Allocation cost is not a measured speed claim; ordinary-stack regression and native timing are gates.
consequences.rollback: Revert the engine presentation change with its decision/evidence; preserve preceding fixes and exact native failure receipts. No data migration or local runtime replacement. Any future atomic display extension requires a separate versioned contract.
consequences.handover: A legacy auxiliary visibility bit inherited by the first Atomic V1 request is inert bookkeeping. Clear selectable authority in every transport, but emit auxiliary clearing only through a transport that supports it. Preserve the bit for later legacy lifecycle cleanup; never send a legacy effect outside an atomic frame. Native panel cleanup across transport handover is not yet tested.
consequences.test_inventory_binding: Refresh the test inventory for the new regression tests under the unchanged lane and ignored-test policy, then rebind the existing zero-known-failure contract to it. Preserve failure_count=0, failures=[], the historical observation and all runner validation. The first full run executed all 3219 selected tests with zero failures but correctly returned FAIL because this binding was stale. Obtain a new complete canonical PASS; do not promote that failed receipt or weaken the guard.
